notes.title: Cruelty Squad review: this game is too cool for me, probably
notes.content:
Cruelty Squad didn't click with me, not because of its grinning antagonism or brain grating lofi, but because I didn’t find it all that interesting. I’m sort of rooting for it, still, thumbing its leprous nose-cavity at inexplicable Steam bestsellers that won’t be out for six months.

Still, I signed up to have awful soup, made from Clippy’s wire entrails and melted immersive sim floppy disks, spooned on my eyeballs. What I got was a reasonably tense shooter with some extensively labyrinthine level design and, to be fair, a very good shotgun.

Read more

notes.title: Cruelty Squad is an FPS "set in a sewage infused garbage world"
notes.content:
Cruelty Squad has the aesthetic of early to mid '90s first-person shooters. No, not Doom and Quake. I'm talking about the trash you don't remember. The hyper-violence, the purple lighting, the repeating textures, the art assets rendered at wildly variable resolutions, the faintly cyberpunk themes.

It's out now on Steam and there's a sensorally aggressive trailer below.

Read more

notes.title: Cruelty Squad 1.0 released!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/dec26c662b19028aa70418230b83e54e708d94f8.png[/img]
Cruelty Squad is now finally out of early access!


Changes since the last EA build:

[list]
[*]New level.
[*]New ending.
[*]New weapon.
[*]New unlockable game mode.
[*]Extended organ markets.
[*]Two new implants.
[*]New dialogue for some targets.
[*]Pain.
[/list]

Changes during the early access period:

[list]
[*]Lots of optimization and bug fixing, compared to the initial release it's possible to run the game on much lower end computers.
[*]Controls are smoother, now possible to go up stairs without getting stuck on everything.
[*]6 new levels. (Technically 5 completely new ones, but one was turned into a fully playable level.)
[*]2 new endings.
[*]8 new weapons.
[*]17 new implants.
[*]Hidden new game+ type of thing.
[*]New enemy types.
[*]Stock market simulation.
[*]Organ harvesting integrated with the stock market.
[*]Fishing integrated with the stock market. (70+ different fish to find!)
[*]And lots of other minor things that I can't remember right now.

Big thanks to everyone in the community, and also my friends who have supported me during this development process. This isn't the end, I will continue fixing bugs (I'm sure there's still some I've missed or forgotten to fix) and adding stuff, but the pace will be slower and there will be absolutely no promises of any specific features. Enjoy!

notes.title: Beta Build
notes.content:
Hey everyone. I just released a new beta build of the game. You'll have manually to enable it in the game's settings on Steam. I'm not recommending this version unless you absolutely want to see all the latest content before everyone else, or you actually want to help get the game ready for full release. Consider everything to be work in progress. If you're on the fence I would recommend waiting for the release build to experience the new content.

Differences to the regular build, for now:

[list]
[*]New level, unlocked by beating all the other levels.
[*]New ending.
[/list]

Stuff I want to add before the game is ready for release:

[list]
[*]At least one new weapon.
[*]More fish for the new levels that don't have any yet, including the final one.
[*]More organs for different enemies.
[*]Better representation of in-game companies on the stock market.
[*]Some nice unlockable for beating the game.
[/list]

From now on until release the focus will shift 100% to this beta build, and there will be no changes to the regular one until then. I want the release version to be as bug-free as I can make it, and don't have time to manage multiple builds.

notes.title: Minor patch

Changed the automatic save backups a bit, that's it. All the bigger changes before the full release will happen on an opt-in beta build. I'll hopefully have more news about that next week.

Keep consuming.
CEO, Consumer Softproducts

notes.title: Content Update 1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/2d4bba243774949724c6dd6a573851dbec722c72.png[/img]

Hey everyone. Sorry for the recent lack of information regarding what's going on, I've been working to get this thing done. There's quite a lot of new content, mostly hidden and late game, but also improvements on some stuff that has been complained about.

Changes include:
[list]
[*]Fixed player getting stuck on polygon seams with high frames per second. The movement should be more even between different computers in general.
[*]Fixed getting stuck on stairs. Somewhat related to above.
[*]Added a suicide button for people who are impatient to retry after dying.
[*]New music tracks for some of the levels that still didn't have them.
[*]Changes to level 1 music as it was incredibly grating and frustrating to some new players.
[*]It's now possible to get some money early on.
[*]Two new unlockable hidden levels. They're not as hard to find as the first one but I'm not going to spoil them.
[*]Two new enemies.
[*]Two new weapons.
[*]Some of the weapons are now capable of killing armored enemies.
[*]New implants, both purchasable and hidden.
[*]Added stock market simulation. It's still rough but will be worked on more in the coming updates. Can be accessed during mission.
[*]New ranks for all the levels for beating them with just the starting weapons.
[*]Hidden difficult content.
[*]Numerous small additions and changes.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/da4ba19bf19956db584463dd667431f33e870d75.png[/img]

There's still a lot of work to be done but I think this is a pretty big leap towards what I want the game to be like eventually. Hope you enjoy it!

notes.title: Patch notes 1
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Hope you're having fun with the game. The launch has been way better than expected, both in terms of sales and the extremely positive response. I've especially enjoyed all the speedrun videos I've seen so far and am really looking forward to seeing how those develop.

I decided it would be a good idea to actually release some patch notes to better keep up with what has and hasn't been done. There have actually been a couple of small updates since the launch but I didn't feel like they really warranted individual posts.

Some of the changes:

[list]
[*]You no longer receive fall damage just based on vertical velocity, the game actually checks the fall distance. This prevents weird situations where you just spontaneously receive damage.
[*]Weird full screen toggling issues should now finally be fixed. Full screen status actually saves.
[*]The save reset button has been fixed. It no longer crashes to desktop, and actually clears the save file.
[*]Field of view slider has a visible value.
[*]The K&H X20 aiming no longer has weird twitching. The scope still causes framerate issues, sometimes. I might have to figure out a completely different way to do it or just abandon the functional scope.
[/list]

I'm looking forward to beginning work on new content again after I manage to recover slightly from the launch and no longer have to be on alert for critical issues.

notes.title: Early Access Release!
notes.content:
[h1]WARNING WARNING[/h1]

Felt like this day was never going to come, but I'm really happy to say that Cruelty Squad is now out for purchase. Obviously this doesn't mean that the work is over, being an early access title and all, but it's a really important stepping stone on the way to making the game what I truly want it to be. Already in the current state I think it's fun, extremely replayable and challenging.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/8e61f5e541b86fb2082e95b261b593716677fd18.gif[/img]

My work plan for the early access period is the following:
[list]
[*]Give all targets unique textures and written dialogue.
[*]A couple of levels still don't have their own music, the title screen is also missing a track.
[*]Keep creating new unlockable bonus levels.
[*]New weapons, enemies and equipment.
[*]Add more secret and unique content in the already existing levels.
[*]Persistent changes in the world.
[*]An alternate, "true" ending that requires more than just beating the levels in chronological order.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/29d2b4f06ce229e94398d63bb621c9ba4de0748c.png[/img]

Basically it's mostly going to revolve around playable content, as gameplay wise everything more or less works. I'm going to keep fine tuning things as I see fit, and obviously fixing bugs. I will also be reading feedback and bug reports on the steam discussion section, twitter and discord. Not promising a rigid schedule but progress updates should become more of a regular thing now too.

I'd like to thank the incredibly supportive community, both on twitter and on the community discord, all the testers who gave really good feedback and found incredibly many bugs and issues in a very short amount of time and [url=https://twitter.com/doorofdestinies]@doorofdestinies[/url] for extremely helpful initial work on the sound effects.

I hope you have fun with the game and stick around to see it grow. Remember to drop a review!

notes.title: Early Access Release Date
notes.content:
[h1][b]CONSUMER SOFTPRODUCTS OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/34b4690ee79b3a572e34e043cde67a090099b1c5.png[/img]

Hey everyone!

I haven't updated in a while but it's not because I haven't been working, rather it's because I've been too busy trying to wrap everything up for the early access release. That's right, [b]the game is going to be out on January 4th[/b]. That's the big announcement.

Over the last month or so I've mostly been working on additional content, polishing some of the levels a bit more, getting rid of annoying lingering bugs and improving enemy behaviour. Apparently if you mix up the z and y coordinates when calculating enemy line of sight you won't necessarily notice it for a while, but it makes the enemies really annoying and unpredictable. Very bad for sneaking up behind them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/942f798b06056597f150a76ab6b952bf70a8613c.png[/img]

Some of the stuff I've done since the last update:

[list]
[*]6 new regular levels, a tutorial level and one unlockable bonus level. My original goal was 15 base levels but I realised I'd rather polish the ones I have and work on more secret levels (and other hidden content). I'll try to squeeze in one more bonus level before release but it might not make it. More levels is the primary goal for the early access period.
[*]There's a total of 17 weapons now. Two of them are non-lethal alternative starter weapons, a dart gun and an expandable baton. Non-lethal gameplay is fun but not very fleshed out yet, don't expect to do a completely non-lethal (minus targets) playthrough just yet.
[*]Lots of new equipment, different grenades, armor, speed boosters, jump boosters, double jump item, stealth suits and more. Some of these can be purchased, others have to be discovered in the levels to be unlocked. I'll be adding more of these whenever I can think of something interesting.
[*]Cryptic death mechanics and divine communication.
[*]Performance settings for low-end computers, AI distance and civilian count sliders.
[*]Intro and ending cutscenes.
[*]New enemy types, including the psychosis inducer.
[*]You can now talk to NPCs. There's unique ones who have their own story to tell, generic ones get a random line based on the level.
[*]The game now grades your perfomance depending on level completion time, you can unlock ranks from C to S for each level, S being the best.
[*]Punishment mode. You receive 100% damage (you're as fragile as the enemies) for a hidden benefit.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38524159/1f9d0d6406b8c198b81026a7b689276b704adb73.png[/img]

It's all shaping up really nicely, and I've received a lot of positive feedback from the testers. While the initial early access version won't be exactly the game I want it to be yet, it's close, and I'm looking forward to working on all the stuff I have lined up.

notes.title: Status Update 2
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Progress with the game has been a bit slower for the last few weeks due to non-game development related obligations, I'm hoping to get back on track now that there's nothing distracting me.

Here's what has happened since the last post:

[list]
[*]Got two new levels into a completely playable state and started working on another one. They still need polish but the general layout is done.
[*]Added three new enemies, one with new poison mechanics.
[*]New weapon, an autoshotgun.
[*]Implemented equipment system with purchasable items. (Armor, Skullgun, etc.)
[*]Steamworks integration now works which means the game can actually be released on Steam.
[*]Preliminary support for time based ranking system. (for unlocking cheats etc. special stuff)
[/list]

Other than that I've also done a lot of testing and general tweaking of the gameplay. There's still a lot of work to be done but I feel the game is on a good track to completion, just a matter of putting in the hours. I'm aiming for 15 levels which is more than twice what I have right now, but with each new one I have to spend less time making new assets and programming new game logic so in some ways it's getting faster. The dream is to release something before 2021 but it might be a bit optimistic, we'll see.

notes.title: Discord Server and Development Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone. Some people were asking me about a Discord server for discussing the game so I decided to create one after gauging general interest a bit. So far it has attracted a decent amount of people, come join us if you have questions, want to follow the development process closer or just want to chat with other people interested in the game

Link to the Discord:
https://discord.com/invite/qNDjTTw

The development of the game is progressing smoothly with five levels now in a playable (if unpolished) state. There's still lots of work to do before release and I can't promise any dates yet but it isn't looking too bad right now. Currently I'm working on implementing a shop where you can buy different cybernetic implants to allow for more varied gameplay styles.
